Home Health Nursing/Speech-Language Pathology Visit Note

Patient: 78-year-old male with history of ischemic CVA (right MCA territory) six weeks ago, complicated by moderate oropharyngeal dysphagia confirmed on modified barium swallow study, now residing at home with his daughter as primary caregiver.

Patient remains under the active care of his primary care physician, Dr. R. Alvarez, who continues to monitor his neurologic recovery and swallowing status via home health visits and periodic office follow-up.

Homebound status: Patient requires the assistance of one person and a rolling walker to ambulate even short distances within the home; he becomes markedly fatigued and short of breath after mobilizing more than 10-15 feet. He has not left the home except for two medical appointments transported by wheelchair van since discharge from inpatient rehab. Leaving home requires considerable and taxing effort, consistent with homebound criteria, and this is documented in the chart at each visit.

Face-to-face encounter: Patient was evaluated in person by Dr. Alvarez on the date home health services were initiated for confirmation of ongoing skilled need, well within the required window relative to start of care.

Skilled need: Speech-language pathologist visiting today assessed swallow function and administered surface neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) to the suprahyoid and infrahyoid musculature as part of an ongoing dysphagia rehabilitation program, given persistent difficulty with pharyngeal transit and residue noted on prior instrumental swallow evaluation. Patient tolerated stimulation well at therapeutic intensity without adverse effects. Skilled SLP intervention remains medically necessary given the complexity of the neurogenic dysphagia and risk of aspiration, and this is documented in today's visit note along with objective measures of swallow function (timed water swallow test, oral intake diet level).

Recertification: Home health episode remains within the initial 60-day certification period; no recertification is due at this time, though ongoing need for skilled services is anticipated and will be reassessed accordingly.

Documentation: All findings above are recorded legibly in the patient's electronic medical record and will be available to the A/B MAC upon request, including therapy progress notes and physician communication logs.

Plan: Continue skilled SLP visits 3x/week for continued swallow rehabilitation including surface e-stim as adjunct to exercise-based therapy; reassess swallow function in 2 weeks; caregiver education reinforced on aspiration precautions and modified diet texture.
